data.label: Data movement
data.hint: Copies values between registers, memory and immediates.

stack.label: Stack
stack.hint: Pushes/pops values and maintains the function frame.

cmp.label: Comparison
cmp.hint: Computes and discards the result, keeping only the flags.

sys.label: System
sys.hint: Talks to the kernel or to the hardware.

string.label: Memory blocks
string.hint: Copies, compares and fills whole regions.

mov.name: Move — copies a value
mov.desc: Copies the contents of the source to the destination. The source does not change. There is no memory-to-memory MOV: one of the two sides must be a register (or the source an immediate).
ex: MOV RAX, 10        ; puts the number 10 into RAX
MOV RBX, RAX       ; copies RAX into RBX
MOV [counter], EAX ; writes EAX to the variable counter

movzx.name: Move with Zero eXtend — copies filling with zeros
movzx.desc: Copies a small value (8 or 16 bits) into a larger register, filling the rest with zeros. Use it for unsigned values.
ex: MOVZX EAX, BYTE [buf]  ; 1 byte -> 32 bits, rest zeroed

movsx.name: Move with Sign eXtend — copies preserving the sign
movsx.desc: Same as MOVZX, but replicates the sign bit. Use it for signed values, otherwise -1 in 8 bits becomes 255 in 32 bits.

movsxd.name: Move Sign-Extend Doubleword — 32 to 64 bits with sign
movsxd.desc: Sign-extends a 32-bit value to 64 bits. Very common when an int index is used as a pointer offset.

lea.name: Load Effective Address — computes an address
lea.desc: Computes the address of the expression inside the brackets and stores the number in the destination, WITHOUT reading memory. It is the normal way to take the address of a string, and also a fast way to do arithmetic (multiply by 2/4/8 and add).
ex: LEA RSI, [msg]            ; RSI = address of the string
LEA RAX, [RBX+RCX*4+8]    ; RAX = RBX + RCX*4 + 8, without touching memory
lea.note: MOV RSI, [msg] would read the contents. LEA takes the address.

xchg.name: Exchange — swaps two values
xchg.desc: Swaps the contents of the two operands. When one of them is memory, the operation is atomic (it locks the bus).

cmov.name: Conditional Move — copies only when the condition is true
cmov.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when the condition holds (the same suffix family as the jumps: E, NE, G, L, A, B...). It avoids a branch, which helps the processor not to mispredict.
ex: CMOVL RAX, RBX   ; RAX = min(RAX, RBX)
cmov.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

push.name: Push — pushes a value onto the stack
push.desc: Subtracts 8 from RSP and writes the 64-bit value at that address. The stack grows toward LOWER addresses.
ex: PUSH RAX        ; saves RAX on the stack

pop.name: Pop — pops a value off the stack
pop.desc: Reads 8 bytes from the top of the stack into the destination and adds 8 to RSP. Every PUSH needs a matching POP (or an RSP adjustment) before the RET.

enter.name: Enter — builds the stack frame
enter.desc: Equivalent to PUSH RBP / MOV RBP, RSP / SUB RSP, size. Rarely used today: the hand-written sequence is faster.

leave.name: Leave — tears down the stack frame
leave.desc: Equivalent to MOV RSP, RBP / POP RBP. It is the standard epilogue of a function that used RBP.

add.name: Add — adds
add.flags: Changes CF, OF, SF, ZF, AF, PF.

adc.name: Add with Carry — adds with the carry-in
adc.desc: destination = destination + source + CF. Used to add numbers wider than 64 bits in parts.
adc.flags: Changes CF, OF, SF, ZF, AF, PF.

sub.name: Subtract — subtracts
sub.desc: destination = destination - source. It is also how stack space is reserved: SUB RSP, 32.
ex: SUB RSP, 32   ; opens 32 bytes of local space
sub.flags: Changes CF, OF, SF, ZF, AF, PF.

sbb.name: Subtract with Borrow — subtracts with the borrow
sbb.desc: destination = destination - source - CF. The counterpart of ADC for long numbers.
sbb.flags: Changes CF, OF, SF, ZF, AF, PF.

inc.name: Increment — adds 1
inc.desc: destination = destination + 1. It does not touch CF (unlike ADD x, 1).
inc.flags: Changes OF, SF, ZF, AF, PF. Preserves CF.

dec.name: Decrement — subtracts 1
dec.desc: destination = destination - 1. Widely used in loop counters together with JNZ.
dec.flags: Changes OF, SF, ZF, AF, PF. Preserves CF.

neg.name: Negate — flips the sign
neg.flags: Changes CF, OF, SF, ZF, AF, PF.

mul.name: Multiply (unsigned)
mul.desc: Multiplies RAX by the source. The 128-bit result lands in RDX:RAX. The implicit RAX operand is mandatory.
mul.flags: Changes CF and OF (they tell whether the high part is nonzero).

imul.name: Integer Multiply (signed)
imul.syntax: IMUL source  |  IMUL dest, source  |  IMUL dest, source, immediate
imul.desc: Signed multiplication. The two- or three-operand form is the one used day to day, because the destination is explicit.

div.name: Divide (unsigned)
div.desc: Divides RDX:RAX by the divisor. The quotient goes to RAX and the remainder to RDX. WARNING: clear RDX first (XOR RDX, RDX), otherwise the result is garbage or the CPU raises an exception.

idiv.name: Integer Divide (signed)
idiv.desc: Same as DIV, but signed. Before it, use CQO (64 bits) or CDQ (32 bits) to sign-extend into RDX/EDX.

and.name: AND — bitwise AND
and.desc: Keeps only the bits that are set in both operands. Used to mask (keep just part of the value).
ex: AND RAX, 0x0F     ; keeps only the low 4 bits
and.flags: Clears CF and OF; changes SF, ZF, PF.

or.name: OR — bitwise OR
or.desc: Turns on in the destination every bit that is set in the source. Used to set flags.
or.flags: Clears CF and OF; changes SF, ZF, PF.

xor.name: XOR — exclusive OR
xor.desc: A bit is 1 when the two are different. XOR of a register with itself is the idiomatic (and shortest) way to zero it.
xor.flags: Clears CF and OF; changes SF, ZF, PF.

not.name: NOT — inverts every bit
not.desc: One's complement: every 0 becomes 1 and vice versa.

shl.name: Shift Left — shifts bits to the left
shl.desc: Each shift by 1 multiplies by 2. Zeros come in from the right.
shl.flags: Changes CF (the last bit shifted out), OF, SF, ZF, PF.

sal.name: Shift Arithmetic Left — identical to SHL
sal.desc: The same instruction as SHL; it exists only for symmetry with SAR.

shr.name: Shift Right (unsigned)
shr.desc: Shifts right bringing in zeros. It is the same as dividing unsigned values by 2^n.
shr.flags: Changes CF, OF, SF, ZF, PF.

sar.name: Shift Arithmetic Right (signed)
sar.desc: Shifts right repeating the sign bit, so negative numbers stay negative.
sar.flags: Changes CF, OF, SF, ZF, PF.

rol.name: Rotate Left — rotates to the left
rol.desc: The bits that leave one side enter the other. Nothing is lost.

ror.name: Rotate Right — rotates to the right
ror.desc: Rotation in the opposite direction of ROL.

bt.name: Bit Test — tests a bit
bt.desc: Copies the selected bit into CF without changing the value.

cmp.name: Compare — compares two values
cmp.desc: Computes a - b, throws the result away and keeps only the flags. It is always read together with the following branch: CMP RAX, 10 + JG means "if RAX > 10".
cmp.flags: Changes CF, OF, SF, ZF, AF, PF.

test.name: Test — an AND that only produces flags
test.desc: Computes a AND b and keeps only the flags. TEST RAX, RAX is the idiomatic way to ask "is RAX zero?" — shorter than CMP RAX, 0.
test.flags: Clears CF and OF; changes SF, ZF, PF.

set.name: Set on condition — becomes 0 or 1 according to the condition
set.desc: Writes 1 into the destination byte if the condition is true, otherwise 0. This is how compilers produce a bool.
set.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jmp.name: Jump — unconditional branch
jmp.desc: Continues execution at the given label (or address), with no condition and no return address saved.

loop.name: Loop — repeats using RCX as the counter
loop.desc: Decrements RCX and branches if RCX != 0. Equivalent to DEC RCX / JNZ, but it is usually slower than writing the two.

call.name: Call — calls a function
call.desc: Pushes the address of the next instruction (the return address) and branches to the function. The RET afterwards uses that value to come back.

ret.name: Return — returns from the function
ret.desc: Pops the return address and continues from there. The stack must be exactly as it was on entry, or the return goes to the wrong address.

syscall.name: Syscall — calls the kernel (Linux x86-64)
syscall.desc: Hands control to the kernel. The service number goes in RAX and the arguments in RDI, RSI, RDX, R10, R8, R9. The return value comes back in RAX. RCX and R11 are destroyed.
syscall.flags: Does not change flags (RCX and R11 are overwritten).

int.name: Interrupt — raises a software interrupt
int.desc: INT 0x80 is the old 32-bit Linux system call — in 64-bit code the normal choice is SYSCALL. INT 3 is the breakpoint used by debuggers.

sysenter.name: Sysenter — fast kernel entry (32 bits)
sysenter.desc: Kernel entry mechanism on 32-bit systems. On x86-64 it was replaced by SYSCALL.

cpuid.name: CPUID — identifies the processor
cpuid.desc: Returns CPU information in EAX/EBX/ECX/EDX according to the value previously placed in EAX.

rdtsc.name: RDTSC — reads the cycle counter
rdtsc.desc: Places the number of cycles since reset in EDX:EAX. Used to measure time with high resolution.

hlt.name: Halt — stops the processor
hlt.desc: Only makes sense in kernel/bare-metal code. In a user program it causes a protection fault.

movsb.name: Move String byte
movsb.desc: Copies one byte from [RSI] to [RDI] and advances both. With REP and RCX it is a one-line memcpy.
movsb.flags: Does not change flags. Direction controlled by DF (CLD/STD).

stosb.name: Store String Byte — fills memory with AL
stosb.desc: Stores AL at [RDI] and advances RDI. With REP it becomes a memset.

lodsb.name: Load String Byte — loads a byte from [RSI] into AL
lodsb.desc: Loads one byte from [RSI] into AL and advances RSI. The basis for walking through strings.

scasb.name: Scan String Byte — searches for a byte
scasb.desc: Compares AL with [RDI] and advances. With REPNE it finds a byte inside a buffer (the basis of strlen).

cmpsb.name: Compare String Byte — compares two regions
cmpsb.desc: Compares [RSI] with [RDI] and advances both. With REPE it is a memcmp.

rep.name: REP — repetition prefix
rep.desc: Repeats the string instruction RCX times. REPE stops when ZF=0; REPNE stops when ZF=1.

cld.name: Clear Direction Flag — walk forward
cld.desc: Clears DF: string instructions move forward (RSI/RDI increase). It is the state the ABI expects.

std.name: Set Direction Flag — walk backward
std.desc: Sets DF: string instructions move backward. Always restore it with CLD afterwards.

movss.name: Move Scalar Single — 32-bit float
movss.desc: Moves a single-precision float between XMM registers and memory.

movsd_sse.name: Move Scalar Double — 64-bit double
movsd_sse.desc: Moves a double. Careful: the same MOVSD mnemonic also exists as a string instruction — the assembler decides from the operand.

addsd.name: Add Scalar Double — double addition
addsd.desc: Adds two doubles in XMM registers.
addsd.flags: Does not change the integer flags.

cvtsi2sd.name: Convert Integer to Double
cvtsi2sd.desc: Converts an integer to a double.

nop.name: No Operation — does nothing
nop.desc: Burns one cycle. It is used to align code in memory and as placeholder space for patches.

cdq.name: Convert Doubleword to Quadword — extends EAX into EDX
cdq.desc: Replicates the sign bit of EAX across EDX. Mandatory before a 32-bit IDIV.

cqo.name: Convert Quadword to Octoword — extends RAX into RDX
cqo.desc: The 64-bit version of CDQ. Use it before IDIV with 64-bit operands.

bswap.name: Byte Swap — reverses the byte order
bswap.desc: Converts between little-endian and big-endian (network byte order).

xadd.name: Exchange and Add — swaps and adds (atomic with LOCK)
xadd.desc: Swaps the operands and stores the sum in the destination. The basis of atomic counters.

cmpxchg.name: Compare and Exchange — the x86 CAS
cmpxchg.desc: If destination == RAX, stores the source in the destination; otherwise loads the destination into RAX. The basis of locks and lock-free structures.
cmpxchg.flags: Changes ZF and the other arithmetic flags.

lock.name: LOCK — atomicity prefix
lock.desc: Ensures the memory operation is atomic across cores.

endbr64.name: ENDBR64 — marks a valid indirect branch target
endbr64.desc: Part of the CET/IBT protection. It marks that this address may be the target of an indirect call/jmp. Modern compilers place it at the start of every function.

ud2.name: UD2 — deliberate invalid instruction
ud2.desc: Raises an invalid opcode exception. Compilers use it to mark unreachable code.

je.name: Jump if E — branches when equal
je.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated equal. Flag condition: ZF = 1. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
je.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

sete.name: Set if E — 1 when equal
sete.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when equal (ZF = 1), otherwise 0.
sete.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmove.name: Conditional Move if E
cmove.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when equal (ZF = 1). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmove.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jz.name: Jump if Z — branches when zero
jz.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated zero. Flag condition: ZF = 1. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
jz.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

setz.name: Set if Z — 1 when zero
setz.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when zero (ZF = 1), otherwise 0.
setz.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovz.name: Conditional Move if Z
cmovz.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when zero (ZF = 1). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovz.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jne.name: Jump if NE — branches when not equal
jne.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated not equal. Flag condition: ZF = 0. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
jne.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

setne.name: Set if NE — 1 when not equal
setne.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when not equal (ZF = 0), otherwise 0.
setne.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovne.name: Conditional Move if NE
cmovne.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when not equal (ZF = 0). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovne.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jnz.name: Jump if NZ — branches when not zero
jnz.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated not zero. Flag condition: ZF = 0. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
jnz.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

setnz.name: Set if NZ — 1 when not zero
setnz.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when not zero (ZF = 0), otherwise 0.
setnz.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovnz.name: Conditional Move if NZ
cmovnz.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when not zero (ZF = 0). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovnz.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jg.name: Jump if G — branches when greater (signed)
jg.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated greater (signed). Flag condition: ZF = 0 and SF = OF. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
jg.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

setg.name: Set if G — 1 when greater (signed)
setg.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when greater (signed) (ZF = 0 and SF = OF), otherwise 0.
setg.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovg.name: Conditional Move if G
cmovg.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when greater (signed) (ZF = 0 and SF = OF). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovg.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jge.name: Jump if GE — branches when greater or equal (signed)
jge.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated greater or equal (signed). Flag condition: SF = OF. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
jge.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

setge.name: Set if GE — 1 when greater or equal (signed)
setge.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when greater or equal (signed) (SF = OF), otherwise 0.
setge.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovge.name: Conditional Move if GE
cmovge.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when greater or equal (signed) (SF = OF). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovge.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jl.name: Jump if L — branches when less (signed)
jl.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated less (signed). Flag condition: SF ≠ OF. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
jl.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

setl.name: Set if L — 1 when less (signed)
setl.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when less (signed) (SF ≠ OF), otherwise 0.
setl.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovl.name: Conditional Move if L
cmovl.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when less (signed) (SF ≠ OF). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovl.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jle.name: Jump if LE — branches when less or equal (signed)
jle.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated less or equal (signed). Flag condition: ZF = 1 or SF ≠ OF. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
jle.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

setle.name: Set if LE — 1 when less or equal (signed)
setle.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when less or equal (signed) (ZF = 1 or SF ≠ OF), otherwise 0.
setle.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovle.name: Conditional Move if LE
cmovle.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when less or equal (signed) (ZF = 1 or SF ≠ OF). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovle.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

ja.name: Jump if A — branches when above (unsigned)
ja.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated above (unsigned). Flag condition: CF = 0 and ZF = 0. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
ja.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

seta.name: Set if A — 1 when above (unsigned)
seta.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when above (unsigned) (CF = 0 and ZF = 0), otherwise 0.
seta.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmova.name: Conditional Move if A
cmova.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when above (unsigned) (CF = 0 and ZF = 0). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmova.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jae.name: Jump if AE — branches when above or equal (unsigned)
jae.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated above or equal (unsigned). Flag condition: CF = 0. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
jae.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

setae.name: Set if AE — 1 when above or equal (unsigned)
setae.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when above or equal (unsigned) (CF = 0), otherwise 0.
setae.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovae.name: Conditional Move if AE
cmovae.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when above or equal (unsigned) (CF = 0). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovae.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jb.name: Jump if B — branches when below (unsigned)
jb.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated below (unsigned). Flag condition: CF = 1. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
jb.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

setb.name: Set if B — 1 when below (unsigned)
setb.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when below (unsigned) (CF = 1), otherwise 0.
setb.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovb.name: Conditional Move if B
cmovb.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when below (unsigned) (CF = 1). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovb.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jbe.name: Jump if BE — branches when below or equal (unsigned)
jbe.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated below or equal (unsigned). Flag condition: CF = 1 or ZF = 1. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
jbe.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

setbe.name: Set if BE — 1 when below or equal (unsigned)
setbe.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when below or equal (unsigned) (CF = 1 or ZF = 1), otherwise 0.
setbe.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovbe.name: Conditional Move if BE
cmovbe.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when below or equal (unsigned) (CF = 1 or ZF = 1). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovbe.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

js.name: Jump if S — branches when negative
js.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated negative. Flag condition: SF = 1. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
js.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

sets.name: Set if S — 1 when negative
sets.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when negative (SF = 1), otherwise 0.
sets.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovs.name: Conditional Move if S
cmovs.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when negative (SF = 1). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovs.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jns.name: Jump if NS — branches when non-negative
jns.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated non-negative. Flag condition: SF = 0. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
jns.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

setns.name: Set if NS — 1 when non-negative
setns.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when non-negative (SF = 0), otherwise 0.
setns.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovns.name: Conditional Move if NS
cmovns.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when non-negative (SF = 0). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovns.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jc.name: Jump if C — branches when carry set
jc.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated carry set. Flag condition: CF = 1. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
jc.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

setc.name: Set if C — 1 when carry set
setc.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when carry set (CF = 1), otherwise 0.
setc.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovc.name: Conditional Move if C
cmovc.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when carry set (CF = 1). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovc.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jnc.name: Jump if NC — branches when carry clear
jnc.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated carry clear. Flag condition: CF = 0. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
jnc.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

setnc.name: Set if NC — 1 when carry clear
setnc.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when carry clear (CF = 0), otherwise 0.
setnc.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovnc.name: Conditional Move if NC
cmovnc.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when carry clear (CF = 0). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovnc.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jo.name: Jump if O — branches when overflow set
jo.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated overflow set. Flag condition: OF = 1. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
jo.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

seto.name: Set if O — 1 when overflow set
seto.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when overflow set (OF = 1), otherwise 0.
seto.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovo.name: Conditional Move if O
cmovo.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when overflow set (OF = 1). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovo.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jno.name: Jump if NO — branches when overflow clear
jno.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated overflow clear. Flag condition: OF = 0. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
jno.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

setno.name: Set if NO — 1 when overflow clear
setno.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when overflow clear (OF = 0), otherwise 0.
setno.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovno.name: Conditional Move if NO
cmovno.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when overflow clear (OF = 0). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovno.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jp.name: Jump if P — branches when parity even
jp.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated parity even. Flag condition: PF = 1. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
jp.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

setp.name: Set if P — 1 when parity even
setp.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when parity even (PF = 1), otherwise 0.
setp.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovp.name: Conditional Move if P
cmovp.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when parity even (PF = 1). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovp.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

jnp.name: Jump if NP — branches when parity odd
jnp.desc: Branches to the label when the last comparison indicated parity odd. Flag condition: PF = 0. When the condition is false, execution simply falls through to the next line.
jnp.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

setnp.name: Set if NP — 1 when parity odd
setnp.desc: Puts 1 in the destination byte when parity odd (PF = 0), otherwise 0.
setnp.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

cmovnp.name: Conditional Move if NP
cmovnp.desc: Copies the source to the destination only when parity odd (PF = 0). No branch, so there is no risk of a misprediction.
cmovnp.flags: Reads the flags, does not change them.

movsw.name: Move String word
movsw.desc: Copies one word (2 bytes) from the address in RSI to the address in RDI, then advances both registers by 2 (backwards when the direction flag is set). With the REP prefix it copies RCX words in one instruction — the fastest way to move a buffer, and the usual shape of a memory-copy payload.
movsw.flags: Does not change flags. Direction controlled by DF (CLD/STD).

movsd.name: Move String dword
movsd.desc: Copies one dword (4 bytes) from the address in RSI to the address in RDI, then advances both registers by 4 (backwards when the direction flag is set). With the REP prefix it copies RCX dwords in one instruction — the fastest way to move a buffer, and the usual shape of a memory-copy payload.
movsd.flags: Does not change flags. Direction controlled by DF (CLD/STD).

movsq.name: Move String qword
movsq.desc: Copies one qword (8 bytes) from the address in RSI to the address in RDI, then advances both registers by 8 (backwards when the direction flag is set). With the REP prefix it copies RCX qwords in one instruction — the fastest way to move a buffer, and the usual shape of a memory-copy payload.
movsq.flags: Does not change flags. Direction controlled by DF (CLD/STD).

stosw.name: Store String word
stosw.desc: Stores AX at the address in RDI and advances RDI by 2 (backwards when the direction flag is set). With REP it fills RCX words — how a buffer gets zeroed or filled in one go.

stosd.name: Store String dword
stosd.desc: Stores EAX at the address in RDI and advances RDI by 4 (backwards when the direction flag is set). With REP it fills RCX dwords — how a buffer gets zeroed or filled in one go.

stosq.name: Store String qword
stosq.desc: Stores RAX at the address in RDI and advances RDI by 8 (backwards when the direction flag is set). With REP it fills RCX qwords — how a buffer gets zeroed or filled in one go.

lodsw.name: Load String word
lodsw.desc: Loads one word (2 bytes) from the address in RSI into AX and advances RSI by 2 (backwards when the direction flag is set). Rarely useful with REP: each iteration would overwrite the previous value.

lodsd.name: Load String dword
lodsd.desc: Loads one dword (4 bytes) from the address in RSI into EAX and advances RSI by 4 (backwards when the direction flag is set). Rarely useful with REP: each iteration would overwrite the previous value.

lodsq.name: Load String qword
lodsq.desc: Loads one qword (8 bytes) from the address in RSI into RAX and advances RSI by 8 (backwards when the direction flag is set). Rarely useful with REP: each iteration would overwrite the previous value.

scasw.name: Scan String word
scasw.desc: Compares AX with the word at the address in RDI, sets the flags and advances RDI by 2 (backwards when the direction flag is set). With REPNE it is the classic strlen/strchr loop: it scans until the byte matches or RCX runs out.

scasd.name: Scan String dword
scasd.desc: Compares EAX with the dword at the address in RDI, sets the flags and advances RDI by 4 (backwards when the direction flag is set). With REPNE it is the classic strlen/strchr loop: it scans until the byte matches or RCX runs out.

scasq.name: Scan String qword
scasq.desc: Compares RAX with the qword at the address in RDI, sets the flags and advances RDI by 8 (backwards when the direction flag is set). With REPNE it is the classic strlen/strchr loop: it scans until the byte matches or RCX runs out.

cmpsw.name: Compare String word
cmpsw.desc: Compares the word at [RSI] with the word at [RDI], sets the flags and advances both registers by 2 (backwards when the direction flag is set). With REPE it compares RCX words — memcmp in one instruction.

cmpsd.name: Compare String dword
cmpsd.desc: Compares the dword at [RSI] with the dword at [RDI], sets the flags and advances both registers by 4 (backwards when the direction flag is set). With REPE it compares RCX dwords — memcmp in one instruction.

cmpsq.name: Compare String qword
cmpsq.desc: Compares the qword at [RSI] with the qword at [RDI], sets the flags and advances both registers by 8 (backwards when the direction flag is set). With REPE it compares RCX qwords — memcmp in one instruction.

repnz.name: REP — repetition prefix
repnz.desc: Repeats the string instruction RCX times. REPE stops when ZF=0; REPNE stops when ZF=1.

repz.name: REP — repetition prefix
repz.desc: Repeats the string instruction RCX times. REPE stops when ZF=0; REPNE stops when ZF=1.

repne.name: REP — repetition prefix
repne.desc: Repeats the string instruction RCX times. REPE stops when ZF=0; REPNE stops when ZF=1.

repe.name: REP — repetition prefix
repe.desc: Repeats the string instruction RCX times. REPE stops when ZF=0; REPNE stops when ZF=1.

REG_DOC.rax: Accumulator. Function return value and system call number on Linux.
REG_DOC.rcx: Loop counter; 1st argument on Windows, 4th on Linux. Clobbered by SYSCALL.
REG_DOC.rdx: 3rd argument (Linux) / 2nd (Windows). High half in MUL and DIV.
REG_DOC.rsi: Source in string operations; 2nd argument on Linux.
REG_DOC.rdi: Destination in string operations; 1st argument on Linux.
REG_DOC.rsp: Top-of-stack pointer. Never touch it unless you know what you are doing.
REG_DOC.rbp: Base of the current stack frame; anchors the local variables.
REG_DOC.r10: 4th argument of Linux system calls (in place of RCX).
REG_DOC.rip: Pointer to the next instruction. Only branches change it; [rel x] addressing is relative to it.

FLAG_DOC.ZF: Zero — the result was exactly zero (or the compared values were equal).
FLAG_DOC.SF: Sign — the highest bit of the result is 1 (negative number in signed interpretation).
FLAG_DOC.CF: Carry — a carry-out or borrow happened. It is the flag used by unsigned branches (JA/JB).
FLAG_DOC.OF: Overflow — the result went past the signed range. It is the flag used by signed branches (JG/JL).
FLAG_DOC.PF: Parity — the low byte of the result has an even number of 1 bits.
FLAG_DOC.DF: Direction — defines whether string instructions walk forward (0) or backward (1).
